input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a multi-year take-or-pay minimum (USD 2,000,000 per year for three years) on Customer with express denial of any reduction or termination right — the rule's walk-away position. It also conflicts with Section 9.4 (Customer's termination for convenience on 30 days' notice, paying only for conforming Services provided) and Section 12.3 (Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment). We therefore replaced the commitment with a usage/ordered-services-only payment obligation, consistent with Sections 7.1 and 9.4, and offered the 12-month reducible commitment with true-up as fallback.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment; Customer pays only for Services ordered or used.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitments, so we have replaced the three-year USD 2,000,000 commitment with payment for Services actually ordered or used; this also removes the conflict with our termination-for-convenience right in Section 9.4 and the no-minimum-volume acknowledgement in Section 12.3. If a commitment is commercially essential, we could consider one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued-up rather than penalised.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer has no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, or volume commitment. Customer pays only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form and usage actually incurred, and Customer's termination and reduction rights under this Agreement are unaffected.
